`hassedivisors` adds the Hasse diagram of the divisor lattice of a number, bringing the current catalog from 1236 to 1237 kinds (1238 gallery choices including plain). There is a node for each divisor, in rows by the number of prime factors counted with multiplicity (the rank), 1 at the bottom and the number itself at the top, the nodes of a row in order of their value, centred and nodeSpacing apart; there is an edge from d to e where e is d times a prime (so e covers d: there is no divisor between them). The seed picks the number from 12, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72, 120, 180 and 210, a surface (the tones of the ground, of the edges and of the nodes from rank 0 to the top rank, steps of one ramp, one of four, then shifted together by at most `toneShift`) and one of eight ways of laying the diagram (turned and mirrored). This is mathematics plus my layout (rows 0.7 high, nodes 0.13 apart, radius 0.035, edges 0.005 either side); no outside source was used, the divisor lattice and the cover relation being the definitions of number theory. The set of numbers was chosen: the diagrams of 12 and 18 are each other's mirror image, and those of 60 and 90 are isomorphic, so only one of each is kept; otherwise the picture would not say which number it is. The tests have a separately written model: the divisors, ranks and cover relation by brute force (d divides e with no divisor strictly between), the number of nodes and edges checked against the formulas (the product of the exponents plus one, and the sum of each exponent times the product of the others plus one), the rule of the sampler (an edge to a multiple by a prime) checked against the cover relation, and that the nodes of a row do not touch and the diagram is inside the tile. Every place of the picture (every 0.0037 of a tile), skipping those within 0.0008 of any edge, has the tone, height and roughness that the model gives; the edge of every node in eight directions and both sides of every edge at three places, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile, are exact (checked only where just the boundary being probed is near, since two boundaries within the softened width blend); the tests tell from the picture which number, which way and which surface it is: the tones at the centres of the nodes first, then the tones along every edge (at three places) and at a grid of places (edges are thin and a grid does not see them, which a first version of the test found out: a wrong way passed the grid); the diagrams of 30, 210 (and 36) are their own mirror images, so flipX cannot be told, which the tests allow for and count flipX only when it can be told. Over 1000 seeds every number, every surface and all ways turn up as they should and the tones are shifted over the whole range, and the softening of the edge of a node and of an edge is checked (tolerance 1e-4). Metallic and mortar are 0.

Defaults are a 1 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`dynkindiagrams` adds the Dynkin diagrams of the finite-type root systems, bringing the current catalog from 1237 to 1238 kinds (1239 gallery choices including plain). They are drawn as the Wikipedia article on Dynkin diagrams draws them (**I read the wikitext of the article**): a node for each simple root, a bond of one, two or three parallel lines between nodes that are joined (the multiplicity is the ratio of the squares of the lengths of the roots), on a multiple bond an arrow (a chevron) pointing towards the shorter root (the article notes that some authors reverse this), angles of 180 degrees at a node of two bonds, 120 degrees where D_n forks and 90 degrees where the branch of E_n leaves. The diagrams are the classification: A_n (n from 2 to 8), B_n and C_n (3 to 8), D_n (4 to 8), E_6, E_7, E_8, F_4 and G_2, 29 in all (B_2 is C_2 and A_1 is one node, so they are left out). **Which root of each is the short one is from memory** (I did not read it): in B_n the last, in C_n the last is the long one, in F_4 the last two are short, in G_2 the first. A node is a ring with a filled centre, the nodes nodeSpacing apart, the branch of E_n leaving down from the third node of its chain (5, 6 and 7 nodes in E_6, E_7 and E_8). The seed picks the diagram, a surface (the tones of the ground, of the ink of the bonds and rings, and of the centre of a node, one of four, then shifted together by at most `toneShift`) and lays the diagram along the picture or across it. The tests have a separately written model and check the classification: the number of nodes, the multiplicities of the bonds, the lengths of the roots that the arrows give (the longer is the shorter times the multiplicity), the determinant of the Cartan matrix (A_n: n + 1, B_n and C_n: 2, D_n: 4, E_6: 3, E_7: 2, E_8: 1, F_4: 1, G_2: 1) and that all its leading minors are positive, that the arrow points to the shorter root and that the diagram is inside the tile. Every place of the picture (every 0.0029 of a tile), skipping those within 0.0008 of any boundary, has the tone, height and roughness that the model gives; both edges of every ring in eight directions and both sides of every line and arm of an arrow at three places, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile, are exact (checked only where just the boundary being probed is near); the tests tell from the picture which diagram, which way and which surface it is (the centres of the nodes first, then along every bond and arrow, where the lines of a multiple bond would be, and at a grid: the smaller diagrams are parts of the larger, and the arms of an arrow must reach beyond the lines of the bond to tell B_n from C_n). Over 1000 seeds all 29 diagrams, the four surfaces and both ways turn up about equally often and the tones are shifted over the whole range, and the softening of a ring and a bond is checked (tolerance 1e-4). Metallic and mortar are 0.

Defaults are a 1 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `uarttraces` adds the traces of an asynchronous serial line (UART) as a logic analyser draws them, bringing the current catalog from 1238 to 1239 kinds (1240 gallery choices including plain). There are 8 traces of 64 bit times each; the line is idle high (logic 1); a frame is a start bit (logic 0), eight data bits (least significant first), an even parity bit (it makes the number of ones in the data and the parity bit even) and a stop bit (logic 1), with 1 or 2 idle bits between frames; the first and the last bit of each row are idle, so the picture repeats seamlessly. Each frame holds a byte the seed picks. A level is a line (high at 0.3 of the height of a row, low at 0.7), a change of level is a vertical line at the edge of a bit time, and the edges of the bit times have a faint thin line. The seed picks whether the idle level is drawn high or low (the polarity, as a line of the other polarity such as RS-232 would be drawn), one of four surfaces (the tones of the ground, of the thin lines and of the trace, shifted together by at most `toneShift`) and whether the rows run along the picture or across it. **Source**: the wikitext of the Wikipedia article on the UART, which I read: idle high, the start bit low, the parity bit after all the data bits, the stop bit high, the least significant data bit first in most applications; **the 8E1 configuration is my choice**, and the definition of even parity (the number of ones is even) and that RS-232 uses the other polarity for logic 1 (hence the idle-low drawing) are from memory, not read. The tests have a separately written decoder: it reads the level of every bit time of every row from the picture (where the level line is drawn) and decodes frames by the framing above; every row must be valid (start bit low, parity right, stop bit high, the first and last bit idle, 1 or 2 idle bits between frames, no room left for another frame); the polarity and the way are told by the idle bits; a model built from the decoded levels gives the tone, height and roughness of every place of the picture (every 0.0021 of a tile, skipping those within 0.0008 of any edge) that the sampler gives; the upper and lower edge of the level lines, both sides and both ends of the vertical lines at a change of level and both sides of the thin lines are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile, and the softening is checked at a quarter of the soft width. Over 1000 seeds the four surfaces, both ways and both polarities turn up about half or a quarter of the time each, the tones are shifted over the whole range, and every byte value from 0 to 255 turns up about equally often. Metallic and mortar are 0.

Defaults are a 1 m nominal tile, 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`pigpencipher` adds a sheet of the pigpen (Freemason's) cipher, bringing the current catalog from 1239 to 1240 kinds (1241 gallery choices including plain). It has 8 by 8 places, each with one of the 26 letters as a symbol or a space (27 choices of the seed). The key is the common order that the Wikipedia article on the pigpen cipher names (**I read the wikitext of the article**: grid, grid, X, X; it says that other orders exist, such as grid, X, grid, X, and a Rosicrucian form with one grid of nine places and one to three dots): A to I are the nine places of a tic-tac-toe grid, drawn as the lines of the grid around the place (a place in the top row has no line above it, and so on), J to R the same symbols with a dot, S to V the four places of an X (drawn as the two lines that bound the place), W to Z the same with a dot. **The article gives the key only as an image and does not say in words which letter is in which place**, so the places of A to I in the grid (A top left, B top middle, C top right, D middle left, E middle, F middle right, G bottom left, H bottom middle, I bottom right), the assignment of S top, T left, U right and V bottom in the X, and where the dot is in a place of the X are from my memory, not read; the picture cannot tell which order was used (the key is fixed). A symbol has the half size 0.045 of a tile, the lines the half width 0.0032 and the dot the radius 0.0085 (enlarged so that a cell can be seen). The seed picks the letter of each place and one of four surfaces (the tones of the ground and of the ink, shifted together by at most `toneShift`). The tests have a separately written key: the 26 symbols are made from the rule (which lines of the grid bound a place), and the tests check that they are all different; then every cell is decoded from the picture (the middles of the four sides, the middles of the four lines to the middle, and the places of the dots must all be ground or ink, grid and X symbols must not mix, a space has nothing), and every cell must decode; a model built from the decoded letters gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion of every place of the picture (every 0.0021 of a tile, skipping those within 0.0008 of any edge of a line or dot) that the sampler gives; both sides of every line (in the middle), every end of a line not shared with another line (the ends are round) and the edge of every dot are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile, and the softening of a line of a box, of a diagonal line and of a dot is checked at a quarter of the soft width. Over 1000 seeds each of the 27 symbols (with the space) turns up about 64000 / 27 times (within 250), the four surfaces about a quarter of the time each and the tones are shifted over the whole range. Metallic and mortar are 0.

Defaults are a 1 m nominal tile, 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `ladderlogic` adds a ladder diagram of the ladder logic of programmable controllers, bringing the current catalog from 1240 to 1241 kinds (1242 gallery choices including plain). There are two vertical rails and six rungs in a tile; each rung is a path from the left rail through contacts to one coil at the far right and the right rail. The symbols and their meaning follow the Wikipedia article on ladder logic (**I read the wikitext of the article**): a normally open contact (—[ ]—), a normally closed contact (—[\]—, with a slash), a normally inactive coil (—( )—), a normally active coil (—(\)—, with a slash), and one coil at the far right of a rung. **The article gives the symbols as text, so the drawing is mine, not the article's**: a contact as two bars (in place of the square brackets), where the slash goes, how the two parentheses of a coil are drawn, the places of the rails, the three places on the path of a rung and how a parallel branch is drawn. A rung has three places on its path, each a wire, a normally open contact or a normally closed contact (at least one contact), and may have a parallel branch around one of the places holding one more contact; its coil is the normally inactive or the normally active one. The seed picks the contacts, the branch and the coil of each rung and one of four surfaces (the tones of the ground and of the ink, shifted together by at most `toneShift`). The lines have the half width 0.0032 of a tile. The tests have a separately written decoder: it reads every place of every rung from the picture (the two bars of a contact both ink or both ground, and the middle for a wire or a slash), the branch (the two vertical lines that join it and the contact on it) and the coil (four marks on the two parentheses and the middle for the slash); every probe must be ground or ink and every rung must have a contact; the model rebuilds every line and arc of a parenthesis from the decoded rungs by the rules, and gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion of every place of the picture (every 0.0021 of a tile, skipping those within 0.0008 of any edge) that the sampler gives; both sides of every line, 0.0022 in from both ends of it, both sides of the arcs and beyond both ends of the arcs, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile (only where no other edge is within the softened width), are exact, and the softening is checked at a quarter of the soft width. Over 1000 seeds (6000 rungs) each place is a wire, a normally open contact or a normally closed contact about a third of the time each (the first place 8/27, 19/54 and 19/54, because it takes a contact when a rung would have none), the branch, its place and its contact, and the kind of coil about half or a third of the time each, the four surfaces about a quarter each, and the tones are shifted over the whole range. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`sokobanlevels` adds a Sokoban level of 10 by 10 cells as seen from above, bringing the current catalog from 1241 to 1242 kinds (1243 gallery choices including plain). The rules follow the Wikipedia article on Sokoban (**I read the wikitext of the article**): walls and floor squares; a floor square may be empty, hold the player or hold a box; some floor squares are storage locations, as many as there are boxes, and the aim is to push all the boxes onto storage locations; the player moves one square at a time and can push the box in front of him onto the empty floor square beyond it, but cannot pull. The outer ring of the tile is wall (so the picture repeats as walls between levels), inside each cell is wall with the chance wallChance, and floor that is not joined to the largest connected floor becomes wall; each cell holds a wall (a square a little smaller than the cell, so that the walls show the grid), a storage location (a dot), a box (a square with a cross, in another tone when it stands on a storage location) or the player (a disc, with a ring around it when it stands on a storage location). **The way the levels are made is mine, not the article's**: the boxes (2 or 3) are put on the storage locations and then pulls are made backwards from there, 40 of them (a pull is a push played in reverse: the player stands next to a box and steps back, taking the box with him), so the level can always be solved; if the result has every box on a storage location (the boxes could not be pulled), it is made again with other storage locations, up to 16 times. The seed picks the level and one of three surfaces (seven tones: the ground, the walls, a storage location, a box, a box on a storage location, the player, and the marks of the crosses and rings, shifted together by at most `toneShift`). **The drawing (the cross, the dot, the disc, the ring, the lines between walls) is mine.** The tests have a separately written decoder, which reads every cell from the picture (three probes: the middle, 0.025 to the right of it and at the radius of the ring, which must be one of the seven tones) and the facts of a level (the ring of the tile is wall, one player, as many storage locations as boxes and 2 or 3 of them, every cell that is not a wall joined to the others, at least one box off its storage location, over 300 seeds); **an independent breadth-first solver** (a state is the positions of the boxes and the lowest cell of the region of the player, pushes only, never pulls, and it finds the fewest pushes that put all the boxes on storage locations): it solves every one of 24 levels (the fewest pushes averaging over 6, the largest over 5), and says there is no solution for the same level with a box moved to a dead corner (a corner of walls that is not a storage location); a model built from the decoded level gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion of every place of the picture (every 0.0021 of a tile, skipping those within 0.0008 of any edge) that the sampler gives; the edges of the walls, dots, boxes, crosses (both sides of a diagonal and beyond its end), players and rings are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile (60 seeds, only where no other edge is within the softened width), the softening is checked at a quarter of the soft width, and the height and roughness of the floor, walls, dots, boxes, crosses, players and rings are checked. Over 1000 seeds 2 and 3 boxes turn up about half the time each and the three surfaces about a third each, no level starts solved, some start with a box already on a storage location, each cell inside is floor 70 to 95% of the time and the ring never, a player on a storage location turns up now and then, almost all 1000 levels are different, and the tones are shifted over the whole range. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`starbattleboard` adds a solved one-star Star Battle board (also called Two Not Touch), bringing the current catalog from 1242 to 1243 kinds (1244 gallery choices including plain). It is 8 by 8 squares with exactly one star in every row, every column and every outlined region, and no two stars touching, not even at a corner. **The rules are from the Cluewright guide to one-star Star Battle (I read that page)**: exactly one star in every row, column and outlined region, and stars may not touch, even diagonally; **the other name, Two Not Touch, is only from the snippets of a web search (I did not read that page), and there is no Wikipedia article to read.** The boards are made like this (**my method, not the source's**, and it does not make the solution unique): the stars are put first, row by row, each in a column of a random order that has not been used and is two or more columns from the star of the row above; then the regions grow from the stars: each time the square without a region that has a neighbour in a region and the smallest random number takes the region of a neighbour, until the board is divided. The lines between squares are thin (half width 0.0012, square ends), where two regions meet and around the whole tile they are thick (half width 0.0035); a star is a five-pointed star (outer radius 0.047, inner radius 0.4 of it, one point up) in the middle of its square. The seed picks the board and one of three surfaces (the tones of the ground, the thin lines, the thick lines and the stars, shifted together by at most `toneShift`). The tests have a separately written decoder, which reads from the picture how thick each line is (the tone at the middle of the line is that of a thin or of a thick line) and whether each square has a star, and checks the rules of the board (the frame is thick; a line is thick exactly where the squares on its two sides are in different regions; one star in every column and every row, no two stars touching; the squares joined by thin lines make exactly eight regions, each with one star; 150 seeds) and counts with an independent backtracking counter how many ways there are to put the stars for the regions of each board (at least one, and not every board has just one); a model built from the decoded board gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion of every place of the picture (every 0.0021 of a tile, skipping those within 0.0008 of any edge) that the sampler gives; the edges of the thin lines, the thick lines (including near the ends of a line at the frame) and the stars are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile (only where no other edge is within the softened width), and the softening is checked at a quarter of the soft width. Over 1000 seeds the three surfaces turn up about a third of the time each, each square has a star in about an eighth of the boards (between 50 and 220), almost all boards differ, the largest region is over 12 squares at times, and the tones are shifted over the whole range. Metallic and mortar are 0. **How many solutions each board has, and for how many it is just one, I did not measure; the material is a valid solved board, and does not claim to be a puzzle with a unique solution.**

`debruijnstrips` adds rows of a binary de Bruijn sequence, bringing the current catalog from 1243 to 1244 kinds (1245 gallery choices including plain). There are 32 rows, each a ring of 32 cells, each cell on or off, in which every window of 5 cells in a row (wrapping from the end of the row to its start) is different, so that each of the 32 patterns of 5 cells turns up exactly once. This is the definition of a de Bruijn sequence in the Wikipedia article on de Bruijn sequences (**I read the wikitext of the article**: every string of the length turns up exactly once in the cyclic sequence; they can be made from an Eulerian cycle of a de Bruijn graph). Each row is made like this (**my method**): on the de Bruijn graph (the nodes are the patterns of 4 cells, the edges the patterns of 5 cells), starting from the node of all zeros and taking the two edges out of each node in a random order of the seed, a closed walk through all 32 edges is made (Hierholzer's way); the bits that the edges add, taken in the order that the walk is finished (the reverse of the order of the walk, which is also a de Bruijn sequence, because its windows are the reversed windows) are the row, which is then turned by a random number of cells. An on cell is a square of the half size 0.0144 in the cell. The seed picks each row, one of four surfaces (the tones of the ground and of the on cells, shifted together by at most `toneShift`) and whether the rows run along the picture or across it. The tests have a separately written judge of whether a row is a de Bruijn sequence (the windows of five cells, wrapping round the end of the row, collected in a set, must be 32 different ones) and a decoder from the picture (the tone of every cell must be that of the ground or of an on cell, and both ways round are tried, only the right one making every row a de Bruijn sequence): over 100 seeds every row is one, each row has exactly 16 cells on (it is balanced), the window of all zeros and the window of all ones both turn up, the 32 rows are not all the same, and the judge says that a row with one cell turned over is not one; a model built from the decoded rows gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion of every place of the picture (every 0.0021 of a tile, skipping those within 0.0008 of any edge of a cell) that the sampler gives; the four sides of an on cell are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile (only the sides where the next cell is off), and the softening is checked at a quarter of the soft width. Over 1000 seeds (32000 rows) the four surfaces and both ways turn up about a quarter and a half of the time each, the rows are over 1000 different sequences (counting those that are the same turned as one; there are 2048 of order 5), the start of the window of all zeros in a row is spread over the 32 places (1000 ± 150 each), and the tones are shifted over the whole range. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`redblacktrees` adds a red-black tree of 31 keys drawn from the root down, bringing the current catalog from 1244 to 1245 kinds (1246 gallery choices including plain). The properties follow the Wikipedia article on red-black trees (**I read the wikitext of the article**): every node is red or black, a red node has no red child, and every path from a node to any empty child goes through the same number of black nodes; that the root is black is the fifth requirement of some authors (Cormen et al.) and not required by others (Mehlhorn and Sanders, Sedgewick and Wayne) — **the trees here follow the former: the root is black**. The tree is a binary search tree on the keys 1 to 31: the keys are inserted one at a time in a random order of the seed with the usual insertion (a new node is red, and a red parent is mended by recolouring and rotating); **the insertion is the standard algorithm as I remember it, I did not read the corresponding part of the article against it; and the article does not say how to draw a tree, so the drawing is mine**. A node is a disc of the radius 0.0245, at the place of its key from left to right (the keys spread over the width of the tile between margins of 0.05), at its depth from top to bottom (0.15 per level, closer when the tree is so high that the levels would not fit, from a top margin of 0.06), with a rim of the width 0.004 (an outer disc of the rim tone and an inner, smaller disc of the node tone), a red node drawn in a lighter tone and a black node in a darker one (a pixel has just one tone, so the two colours are told by lighter and darker), and a line of the half width 0.0022 from each node to its parent, behind the discs. The seed picks the tree and one of three surfaces (the tones of the ground, the lines, a red node, a black node and the rims, shifted together by at most `toneShift`). The tests have a separately written decoder (each key's column is scanned from the top down, a disc is a run of the tone of a red or of a black node and its middle is the node; the nodes are grouped into levels by how far down they are; the parent of a node is the one node a level up that has the tone of a line at the points along the line between them that are not under another disc, exactly one) and a separately written checker of the properties: exactly one root and it is black, the binary search tree property (the in-order walk is exactly 1 to 31), no red node with a red child, the same number of black nodes on every path to an empty child, and the height equal to the number of levels and not over 2 log2(n + 1); all 150 seeds pass, and the checker complains about a tree with a red node turned black; a model built from the decoded tree gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion of every place of the picture (every 0.0021 of a tile, skipping those within 0.0008 of any edge) that the sampler gives; the outer and inner edge of every disc and both sides of every line are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile (only where no other edge is within the softened width), and the softening of the outer edge, the inner edge and the lines is checked at a quarter of the soft width. Over 1000 seeds the three surfaces turn up about a third each, the 1000 trees are almost all different, their heights are between 5 and 10 levels and not all the same, every one is a red-black tree, and the tones are shifted over the whole range. There are about 15 red nodes in a tree (about half). Metallic and mortar are 0.

`i2ctransactions` (transactions on an I2C bus) brings the current catalog from 1245 to 1246 kinds (1247 gallery choices including plain). Each row draws the two lines of an I2C bus, SCL (the clock) on the top half and SDA (the data) on the bottom half, as a logic analyser does. The rules follow the Wikipedia article on I2C (**I read the wikitext of the relevant parts of the article**): both lines are high when idle; START is SDA going from high to low while SCL is high; then the 7-bit address of the target and a read/write bit (0 write, 1 read), and the target answers with an ACK bit (0); then one or two data bytes, each followed by an acknowledge bit (for a write the target sends a 0; for a read the controller sends a 0, **except after the last byte, where it sends a 1 (NACK)**); the address and the data are most significant bit first; a bit is one pulse of SCL (low for half of a clock, then high for the other half) with SDA held, every other change of SDA is while SCL is low; STOP is SDA going from low to high while SCL is high. The addresses are the ones that are not reserved, 8 to 119 (the article says two groups of 8 addresses are reserved and 112 remain; **that the reserved ones are 0 to 7 and 120 to 127 is my reading of "112 remain", I did not read the address table of the article**); each byte is that of the seed. **The drawing is mine**: a row has 64 cells (half a clock each), the first cell idle and the message starting from the second, so every row begins and ends idle and the tile repeats; the message can be anywhere in the row from the second cell until its STOP is in the last one (24 places for a message of one data byte, 6 for two); SDA changes at the moment SCL falls, drawn as a vertical line on the same cell boundary, which is the idealised way a timing diagram is drawn and not a rise time and a hold time; clock stretching, repeated START and 10-bit addresses are not drawn. Each clock has a thin line at its edge, a level is a horizontal line of the half width 0.0032 (high at 0.1 / 0.6 of the height of the row, low at 0.4 / 0.9), a change of level is a vertical line, and the seed picks whether the high level is drawn up or down, whether the rows run along the picture or across it, and one of four surfaces (the tones of the ground, the thin lines, SCL and SDA, shifted together by at most `toneShift`). SCL and SDA have different tones, so they can be told apart in the picture. The tests have a separately written reader of the picture (the way, the polarity, the surface and the level of each line in every cell, and the thin lines and vertical lines are checked) and an I2C decoder written from the Wikipedia article (the START and STOP conditions, a bit taken at the rise of SCL, the address and data most significant bit first, the acknowledge bits, the last pulse before the STOP not being a bit; exactly one message in a row; every byte of a write acknowledged, the last byte of a read answered with a 1); every row of 60 seeds decodes, the address is 8 to 119, one or two bytes, and the number of cells from START to STOP is right; the decoder complains about a broken message (an address that is not acknowledged, SDA moving while the clock is high, no STOP, the acknowledge after the last byte of a read the wrong way round); a model gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion at every place of the picture (away from any edge by 0.0008) that the sampler gives; the upper and lower edge of the level lines, both sides and both ends of the vertical lines and both sides of the thin lines are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile, and softened over a quarter of the soft width; over 1000 seeds the four surfaces, the two ways round and the two polarities turn up equally often, the addresses, reads and writes, one and two bytes are spread, every bit of the data is about half ones, the messages start at every possible place, every byte value 0 to 255 turns up, and the tones are shifted over the whole range. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`hamiltoniancycles` (Hamiltonian cycles) brings the current catalog from 1246 to 1247 kinds (1248 gallery choices including plain). It is a closed line along the grid through every vertex of a square grid exactly once (a Hamiltonian cycle). **The construction is the usual one as I remember it; I did not read it from any source, and its correctness rests on the separately written checker of the tests, not on a source**: the grid is cut into blocks of 2 by 2 vertices, each a cycle of four edges; a random spanning tree of the blocks (Kruskal, the edges in the order of a hash of the seed) is made, and for each tree edge the two sides of the blocks that face each other are replaced by the two edges between the blocks, which makes the two cycles one; when all the tree edges are done there is one cycle through every vertex. The grid needs an even number of vertices on a side (the grid graph is bipartite, which is my own knowledge of the mathematics, I did not look it up). The seed picks a side of 12, 16 or 20 vertices; the pitch is 1 / side and the vertices are at (i + 0.5) pitches, so the cycle does not touch the cycles of the tiles around it; a vertex is a bead of the radius 0.27 of the pitch and an edge a line of the half width 0.21 of the pitch (drawn under the beads); the seed picks the cycle, the size and one of four surfaces (the tones of the ground, the line and the beads, shifted together by at most `toneShift`). The tests have a separately written reader of the picture (the corner of the tile is the ground, a vertex has the bead tone, the middle of two neighbouring vertices decides the edge by being the line tone or the ground, the middle of every square and the places across the tile boundary are the ground; the three sizes are tried and exactly one must be valid) and a checker written from the definition (every vertex has exactly two edges and a walk from the vertex in the corner comes back after exactly as many steps as there are vertices, so it is a single cycle); all 150 seeds are a single cycle with as many edges as vertices, all three sizes turn up and the 150 cycles are all different; the checker complains about a picture with an edge missing and about the picture in which every 2 by 2 block is its own cycle (every vertex also has two edges there, but it is not a single cycle); a model gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion at every place of the picture (away from any edge by 0.0008) that the sampler gives; the circle of a bead and the sides of a line are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile, and softened over a quarter of the soft width; over 1000 seeds the three sizes and the four surfaces turn up about equally often, all 1000 cycles are different, for the smallest grid each of the 60 pairs of neighbouring blocks is joined in between 30% and 85% of the cycles (a spanning tree takes 35 of the 60 edges, so about 58%), and the tones are shifted over the whole range. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`postnetbarcodes` (POSTNET postal barcodes) brings the current catalog from 1247 to 1248 kinds (1249 gallery choices including plain). Each row draws one POSTNET barcode, the barcode the United States Postal Service used to print on letters. The rules follow the Wikipedia article on POSTNET (**I read the wikitext of the article**): the barcode has a full-height frame bar at the start and at the end; each digit is five bars of which two are full height and the others half height (a two-out-of-five code), the five places have the weights 7, 4, 2, 1, 0 from left to right, the weights of the full bars add up to the digit, and zero adds up to 11; after the digits there is a check digit that makes the sum of all the digits, including the check digit, a multiple of 10; the article names the formats of 5 digits (the A code, 32 bars), 6 (the B code, 37 bars), 9 (the C code, 52 bars) and 11 (the delivery point code, 62 bars), all with the check digit. The table of the article (the bars of the digits 0 to 9) is written out in `codes` and the **example 55555-1237, whose check digit is 2**, is also a test. **What I decided**: a row has 64 slots (the bars are 1/64 of a tile apart), each row picks one of the four formats, its digits from the seed, and a start anywhere that keeps the first and the last slot empty; a bar has the half width 0.0031, full and half bars are in the ratio 5 to 2 in height (that is the ratio of the real bars as I remember them, about 0.125 and 0.05 of an inch; the article gives no sizes, so the heights are my choice); the seed picks the way round (the rows along the picture or across it), whether the bars rise from the baseline or hang from it, and one of four surfaces (the tones of the paper and the ink, shifted together by at most `toneShift`). The tests have a separately written reader of the picture (each slot is probed in the middle of the bar, between the tops of the full and the half bars, above the full bars and below the baseline, and must be exactly ink or paper; a bar is none, half or full) and a barcode reader written from the article (the frame bars, exactly two full bars in every five, the weights 7, 4, 2, 1, 0 with 11 as 0, the digits adding up to a multiple of 10); every row of 100 seeds decodes and all four formats turn up; the reader complains about a broken barcode (a digit with three full bars, a changed check digit, a frame bar that is a half bar); a model gives the tone, height, roughness and occlusion at every place of the picture (away from any edge by 0.0008) that the sampler gives; the sides, the tops and the baselines of the bars are exact, just inside and just outside by 0.0004 of a tile, and the tone, the height and the roughness are checked at a quarter of the soft width; over 1000 seeds the four surfaces, the two ways round and the two baselines turn up about equally often, the four formats about a quarter each, the digits 0 to 9 about a tenth each, the starts of every format cover every place there is room for, and the tones are shifted over the whole range. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`to92packagefaces` adds four rotated/jittered 2×2 TO-92 front schematics, bringing the current catalog from 885 to 886 kinds (887 gallery choices including plain). Matte-black D-shaped bodies have straight sides, flat bottoms and upper elliptical domes; three equally spaced parallel straight neutral-metal leads have broad root shoulders and narrow tails, with roots masked by the body. No exposed tab, mounting hole or markings are drawn. Full leads have M1; body/backing have M0, with C1 boundary blends. Authored normalized heights are backing .02 < lead .44 < body .68.

The dimension reference is the actually downloaded and raster-viewed [onsemi P2N2222A/D, January 2013 Rev. 7, PDF page 6](https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/p2n2222a-d.pdf#page=6): embedded drawing 98ASB42022B, TO-92 (TO-226), CASE 29-11, Issue AM, dated 09 MAR 2007, drawing page 1 of 2, STRAIGHT LEAD BULK PACK view. Its A 4.45–5.20 mm, B 4.32–5.33 mm, G 1.15–1.39 mm and K ≥12.70 mm are dimension references only, not measurements of the artwork. The upper half ellipse, proportions, shoulders, color, roughness, AO and heights are authored simplifications, not exact CAD. No chemistry, plating, optical or electrical properties are inferred; no source artwork is shipped.

Defaults are a 0.08 m nominal tile, 0.0042 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 1. Explicit `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` changes only the scalar factor, not the stored M mask. The TO-220 constructor-cached pose/grain and C1 role-replacement structure is reused, preserving periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership without new APIs or dependencies. Remove borrowed materials before destroying the texture-owning preset; manage caller-owned pools/caches separately. Prefer 512 for the three narrow tails; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim runtime/browser verification.

`ftypefemalefaces` adds four 2×2 bare F-type female bulkhead front schematics, bringing the catalog from 883 to 884 kinds: six-flat nickel-plated metal hex bases, concentric raised round shoulders, CLOSED unkeyed raised circular lips, pale P.P. dielectric disks and tiny deeper dark opaque central female entries. Exterior hardware has M1; backing, P.P. and entries have M0. Authored normalized height order is backing .02 < entry .06 < nut .26 < shoulder .36 < P.P. .48 < lip .66. The entry is a height depression, not a painted dot; pale P.P. remains continuous around it. Unlike ST, there is no open keyway or bayonet stud, and no male pin or invented visible central metal contact ring.

The primary reference is the actually downloaded and raster-viewed historical [Amphenol Connex CAT-103 ©2001 catalog, PDF page 159 / printed page 158](https://docs.rs-online.com/1ab7/A700000006717073.pdf#page=159): the 222121 BULKHEAD ADAPTER JACK-TO-JACK photograph, drawing and model-specific Nickel / P.P. / 75Ω table. Generic Delrin/Teflon notes elsewhere do not override this model's P.P.; neither base-alloy chemistry nor exact contact material is inferred. The drawing's 11 HEX and 21.3 mm axial overall length are references, not measured front geometry; washer/nut side dimensions are not front height. The tiny actual entry cross-section is unresolved at source-photo resolution: its circular form here is a deliberate artist simplification, not exact CAD. Proportions, color, roughness, AO, layer heights, default 0.04 m tile and 0.0042 UV-relief factor are authored; .0042 is not metres or a calibrated depth. No thread helix/decorative thread turns, washer teeth, rear/cable/PCB, real holes, transparency or new mesh; no RF/75Ω, electrical, optical, mating or safety simulation/certification. Historical 75Ω identifies the part only. Source assets are not bundled; this extends the existing `pbr3d` gallery, not a new examples entry.

The independent 46-field preset (44 numeric fields and two palettes) uses ten C1 profiles: six smooth hex half-planes and four squared-radius circle profiles. Nested convex role replacement and 20 constructor-cached C/H/R/AO deltas avoid nonzero hard-min/max joins. Four four-column Float64 poses (128 B) plus 96² Float64 grain (73,728 B) retain 73,856 B typed-array payload, excluding JS object/closure overhead—not total RAM, FPS or a performance improvement claim. The rotation-independent owner bound, maxScale × nutInradius / (sqrt(3)/2) + jitter, is approximately .369958 < .5. Constructor-cached poses/grain leave no query allocation, loop, hash, trigonometry or square root; zero support and unused grain on full P.P./entry/backing are skipped. The second fractional wrap before owner indexing is retained for tiny negative UVs. Default metallic is 1; explicit `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` changes only the factor, not the stored hardware/nonmetal mask. Existing opaque four maps, optional height, tint/repeats and sync/Worker/cache APIs and ownership remain unchanged: remove borrowing materials before disposing the texture-owning preset, and manage caller-owned pools/caches separately. No new dependency or API. These are source/implementation descriptions, not full-suite, runtime, browser or built-distribution verification claims.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('ftypefemalefaces', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`. Prefer 512 for the pale disk and tiny recessed entry; 32 is a coarse preview, not a guarantee that the entry resolves. Explicit `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` retains the stored mask and existing texture ownership/cleanup.

`rcafemalefaces` adds four 2×2 RCA/Cinch female-face schematics: broad round black insulating washers, smaller round metal shoulders, still smaller six-flat front barrel noses, dark annular insulators and deep round bores with simplified recessed conductive socket annuli and dark opaque floors. There are no BNC bayonet lugs, male center pins or large rear mounting nuts on the front. This is a connector-family variation, not new rendering or connector-simulation technology.

Appearance references actually read/viewed: the primary [REAN NYS367-0 drawing](https://www.rean-connectors.com/media/14879/download/NYS367-0.pdf?v=1), drawing 3.652.052 dated 2020-11-13, and the generic [NYS367 product PDF](https://www.rean-connectors.com/en/product/nys367-1.pdf). The drawing labels washer Ø15.5, barrel Ø8.3, front length 7.5, M8×0.75 and overall (29); AF12 describes the large rear nut, not a front measurement. Its inconsistent NYS373-x note is not evidence for a new variant, and the product PDF URL is not evidence of a NYS367-1 variant. Product photographs show the small front flats, wider washer and rear nut/lug; the PDF lists brass/gold housing, nut, lug and pin and PA+30%GF washer, not a specified inner dielectric resin. Neutral gray deliberately omits real gold optics; all shapes, positions, relief, palette, roughness and the 0.04 m nominal tile / 0.0042 UV relief are authored approximations, not measured CAD, tolerances or a hidden cross-section.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('rcafemalefaces', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`. Prefer 512 for the six-flat barrel and recessed female socket; 32 is only a coarse preview. Default metallic 1 retains the metal/nonmetal map; `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` changes the factor, not the stored map. Keep existing opaque four maps, optional height, tint/repeats, synchronous/module Worker pool/cache and preset-owned texture lifetimes: remove borrowing materials before destroying the preset, and manage caller-owned pools/caches separately. The independent 56-field preset/kernel combines six radial squared-distance C1 profiles with three smooth folded hex slabs and 27 cached channel deltas. Four four-column poses (128 B) and 96² Float64 grain (73,728 B) retain 73,856 typed-array payload bytes, not total RAM or FPS. The charcoal palette and complete grid are authored, with no copied image asset or specific TI/Intel part, pinout, JEDEC dimensions, solder alloy, assembly/reflow/reliability or electrical certification. Reused cached-noise and compact C1 owner conventions retain 128 B of four poses plus 128² grain, 131,200 B of typed tables, not total RAM or FPS. Default per-axis owner support is 0.34√2 + 0.012 = 0.492833 < 0.5; ball radius 0.0125 is below half the 0.04 pitch. Nearest row/column lookup evaluates only one ball, never scans the array. Owner floors are computed once per axis; sampling allocates nothing and performs no hash, square root, trigonometry or neighbor search. Paired signed half-plane products preserve C1 carrier corners, ball supports vanish before nearest-grid owner boundaries, and continuous grain does not jump with grid ownership. Maps retain metallic 1 on balls and 0 on carriers/backing; default factor 1 preserves mixed metal, while explicit 0 changes only the factor. The 0.05 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV relief are authored, not metre-valued depth or dimensional calibration. Inventory grows from 862 to 863; existing opaque four maps/optional min–max height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership remain unchanged, without real ball meshes, underfill/routing, solder flow, transparency or additional browser/Canvas2D certification.

`pigskinleather` adds warm-brown matte skin with 64 irregular triangular follicle triplets: each group contains three separate rounded pits whose centers are lower, darker, rougher and occluded. Seeds vary group placement/orientation/radius and individual pore size/ellipse orientation. The arrangement is triangular, not each individual pore. It is distinct from existing Voronoi-pebbled `leather`, single raised quill collars in `ostrichleather`, hairy `cowhide` patches and the equal-sized single staggered perforations of `perforatedleather`. References actually read are [Etherington and Roberts' conservation dictionary, pigskin](https://cool.culturalheritage.org/don/dt/dt2578.html), [Kawanishi Kaban's ∴ identification paragraph](https://shop.kawanishikaban.com/en/blogs/%E7%B4%A0%E6%9D%90%E3%81%AB%E3%81%A4%E3%81%84%E3%81%A6/material-pigskin), and the [Leather Repair Company pigskin entry](https://prorestorers.co.uk/knowledgebase/pig-leather-skin/). Two 300px close-ups from the latter were viewed, but are not used to certify every triplet visually. The dictionary's roughly triangular groups of three inform an authored motif, not authenticity, breed, tanning, Nappa grading or pore-density certification. Existing cached-noise, compact C1 cavity and single-owner table patterns are reused: three bounded elliptical pits over continuous two-scale grain, not a new general leather API. The 192 × 5 center/quadratic coefficients plus 64² + 128² grain values retain 171,520 typed bytes, excluding JS objects, output maps and total RAM. Sampling visits exactly three pores without allocation, hashing, square roots, trigonometry or neighbor scanning. Default per-axis support is bounded by 0.426782 < 0.5, while within-triplet pore-center distance ≤0.250337 remains below the inter-triplet lower bound 0.272686. The nominal 0.028 m tile and relief 0.0038 UV units are authored, not measured pore depth. Opaque dielectric maps do not reconstruct through-dermis follicles, the flesh side, wrinkle networks, breathability or transmission.

`diatomvalves` depicts four seeded ivory, lanceolate external valve motifs: apically elongated lineolae form paired transapical striae around an expanded, flush central clear area, while two raphes remain separated centrally and bend slightly toward the same side near their tips. The axial sternum rises slightly; pores and fissures are lower, darker, rougher and occluded, not eight chiton plates, guard-cell rings or deep internal-valve chambers. References actually read include the [Diatoms of North America Navicula guide](https://diatoms.org/genera/navicula/guide), [N. tripunctata external/internal SEM metadata](https://diatoms.org/species/navicula_tripunctata/images), and the morphology section/caption of [Yılmaz et al. (2024), Fig.3](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11019260/). Both tripunctata SEM views and Fig.3 were actually viewed: A–D are external, E–H internal; internal grooves/helictoglossae are not copied onto the outer face. This is an authored naviculoid motif, not a species reconstruction, SEM gold coating, live cell or complete paired frustule. The 0.00012 m tile, 2² layout, ivory palette and exaggerated normal-authoring relief 0.0022 are not calibrated pore density, shell thickness or reflectance. Existing cached poses, C1 compact support and grain support bounded nearest-row/column lookup of one lineola; construction retains four poses, 24 row bounds and 96² grain, totaling 160 + 768 + 73,728 = 74,656 typed bytes, excluding JS/output maps and without claiming an fps gain. Whole aperture supports stay outside the central clear area instead of per-pixel clipping into split fragments. Default radius plus jitter is 0.47070 < 0.5 cell; row/column switches occur outside aperture support. Sampling allocates nothing and uses no hash, sqrt, trig, neighboring-cell or per-pore scan. Fully opaque M0 cavities retain solid backing; no geometry, transparency/transmission, full girdle/internal valve, photonics, locomotion or biological model is added.

`chitonshells` adds nine elongated oval dorsal motifs, each with eight raised valves (two terminal caps and six intermediate plates), seven directionally asymmetric lap shoulders and a darker, rougher mantle girdle around the shell core. Exposed faces rise in the lap direction beneath a low rounded midline ridge; a continuous lower, darker, occluded shell underface remains at the seams, rather than merely incising seven symmetric lines into one oval. [UCMP Polyplacophora](https://ucmp.berkeley.edu/taxa/inverts/mollusca/polyplacophora.php), including the actually viewed Lined Chiton photograph/anatomy diagram, informs the eight dorsal plates and girdle. The actually viewed dorsal/side SEM in [Connors et al. (2019), Fig. 1a–b](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6904579/) distinguishes the eight primary plates from the peripheral small scales. This preset only grains the girdle; it does not reconstruct that paper's hundreds of scales or μ-CT geometry. The warm-brown palette, 0.12 m tile and 3² layout are authored illustration, not grayscale-SEM color recovery, a particular species or calibrated biological scale. Existing compact squared ellipse shoulders and C1 corner-ramp conventions form rounded-absolute chevrons. One owner and one active course suffice, without scanning eight plates per pixel. The constructor precomputes hashes, rotation/scale bases, plate tones and 96² grain; poses/tones 864 B + grain 73,728 B retain 74,592 B of typed storage, excluding JS/output maps and not proving higher fps. Default maximal rotated radius plus jitter is 0.47335 < 0.5. Curved coordinates can extend beyond the last interval inside the tail cap: retain its last valve rather than read the next owner's tone or undefined. The field hot path has no allocation, hashing, square roots or trigonometry; shoulders and ramps remain C1. This fully opaque dielectric 2D relief does not create hidden overlap volumes, eight articulated meshes, rolling motion, shell-eye optics, transmission/SSS, shell-layer/muscle anatomy or biomechanics.

`leafstomata` depicts 25 schematic pairs of kidney-shaped guard cells with seeded size, position, orientation and pore-width variation around dark, recessed, occluded opaque pore floors. The two brighter, smoother cell crests meet at slightly lower polar contacts that remain above the leaf ground; this is not an undivided shell rim, toothed cowrie aperture or single coffee-bean groove. The actually read [Nadeau and Sack (2002), Stomatal Development in Arabidopsis](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3243354/), including its viewed Fig. 1 TEM/cryo-SEM, and [Jaafar and Anderson (2024), stomatal cell-wall review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232514/), including its viewed Fig. 1 schematic, inform kidney-shaped eudicot guard cells joined at their poles rather than grass dumbbells. These are a reference chapter/review and their cited images, not experiments reproduced by the engine. The 0.00025 m tile, 5² layout and green palette are authored illustration, not colors measured from grayscale SEM, calibrated stomatal density or a species reconstruction. Existing compact squared shoulders and cached grain support C1 outer/pore shoulders, radial crests and polar contacts; the full pore skips the undefined radial coordinate. The constructor precomputes hashes, rotation/scale bases, inverse pore widths and 96² grain/12² skin noise. The field hot path has no allocation, hashing, square roots or trigonometry. Poses 1,200 B + grain 73,728 B + skin 1,152 B retain 76,080 B of typed storage, excluding JS containers/output maps and not proving higher fps. Default rotated support plus jitter has conservative half-width 0.448 < 0.5, requiring only its owner. Rough green ground abstracts the epidermis; it does not reconstruct pavement-cell topology, the developmental one-cell-spacing rule, organelles, geometric air passages, transmission/SSS, live opening, transpiration or biomechanics.

It is not fruit-rind striping, recolored cubic fluorite or engraved inlay. `cuttlebone` adds a warm-white, rough dielectric wall–septa section over dark, recessed, occluded opaque backing. The actually read [Yang et al. (2020) wall–septa study and Fig. 1](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7519314/), including its SEM/reconstruction images, provide the visual reference: cuttlebone is an internal shell, not vertebrate bone. The authored 0.0024 m nominal tile has six uneven layers and 24 staggered, oppositely bending, variable-amplitude quintic supports per layer, joined to septa by C1 product union—not a white recoloring of the continuous transverse medium in `cardboardedge`. This is a schematic 2D section; real 3D walls form a branching open labyrinth, so 144 2D windows do not mean 144 sealed chambers or the paper’s 93 vol% porosity. It does not reconstruct micro-CT, the 3D waviness gradient/growth direction, geometric holes, transmission/SSS, buoyancy, strength or biological dimensions. `pallasite` adds an opaque polished-slice approximation: olive-to-honey dielectric crystals in a connected silver-gray metallic matrix, nearly coplanar phases and fine darker, slightly recessed, rougher intramineral fissures—not raised pebbles or cement grout. The actually read [NASA Mittlefehldt/Rumble abstract](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20060020744/downloads/20060020744.pdf) describes magnesian olivine mixed with iron-nickel, and [ASU’s Buseck Center](https://meteorites.asu.edu/stony-iron-meteorites/pallasites) describes greenish olivine; the [Esquel slice photo](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/Esquel.jpg) was viewed for crystal/reflective-metal morphology, not copied. This front-lit opaque authored PBR model does not provide the photo’s backlit transmission, refraction, gem quality, calibrated iron-nickel optical constants, etched Widmanstätten structure or origin/composition certification. The 0.16 m tile has 8² jittered periodic Voronoi grains, varying erosion and C1 half-plane products. Clipping, hashing, square roots and trigonometry run only during construction; pixels inspect a 3² owner patch and surviving facets without allocating arrays/objects or rebuilding polygons, stopping at the first disjoint positive support. Across three sampled seeds each tile has 384 unit-plane triplets, four to eight facets per grain and mean six; retained typed storage including 96² grain is 88,064 B and shared construction scratch 1,608 B, excluding JS containers/output maps—not FPS. Seed changes crystal placement, size, tone and fissures. Grains M0/matrix M1 use the existing neutral-matrix pigment path; default metallic factor 1 preserves the mask, explicit 0 makes both dielectric. Four opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, sync/Worker/cache and ownership remain; no dependency, entry point, mesh, Canvas2D or cross-browser certification is added.

`gosperinlay` adds one slightly raised, smoother brass-toned metallic line over a rough navy dielectric backing. The [Gosper curve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gosper_curve) page and its raw wikitext supply the 60° turtle, axiom A and both A/B productions. Three offline expansions give 343 equal links and 344 distinct triangular-lattice vertices, with two endpoints, no branches and no closing edge: a finite order-three pattern, not the limiting space-filling set or a Gosper-island tessellation. This differs from `moorecurve`’s 64-cell orthogonal closed groove, `boullebrassinlay`’s S-shaped foliate scrolls and `kintsugiceramic`’s crack network. Its 0.5 m preset stores a 343-character direction word. Construction builds four-value segments and 16² local bbox buckets; pixels do not interpret an L-system, allocate arrays/objects, scan all 343 links or use sqrt/trig/hash. It reuses `vogelspiral`’s in-place prefix-end indexing and `fiddleheads`’ product-union rounded joins: 801 references, 257 offsets, at most eleven candidates and a whole-tile mean of 3.12890625 per bin; typed storage including the 96² Float64 grain is 86,820 B, excluding JS strings/objects/output maps. These are structural counts, not FPS measurements. Squared capsule distance and C1 cubic shoulders retain round caps and flat cores. Seed affects grain finish only, not path placement or metal classification. Line M1/backing M0 needs a default material metallic factor of 1; explicit 0 makes both dielectric. Four opaque PBR maps, optional height and existing tint/repeats, sync/Worker/cache and ownership remain. No new entry point, dependency, mesh, alloy/conductivity/manufacturing simulation, Canvas2D or untested-browser certification.

`vogelspiral` is a finite golden-angle panel of 97 equal flat glazed disks with rounded shoulders above rough gray backing, in teal/sage/ivory families of 33/32/32. The actually read [Vogel phyllotaxis section of Fermat’s spiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermat%27s_spiral#The_golden_ratio_and_the_golden_angle) gives r=c√n and θ=n×137.508°. This authored variant explicitly uses r=0.044√(n+0.5), θ=nπ(3−√5), n=0–96: the half-step radial offset avoids central crowding and is not the original n=0 center. These are discrete equal disks, not a continuous spiral, tangent growing-radius Doyle spirals, a plant simulation or certified Fibonacci arm counts. The nominal 0.5 m tile has UV radius 0.033 (nominally 16.5 mm); minimum center distance 0.06802551 exceeds diameter 0.066, with outer support radius 0.46523142 and clear margins, not an installation certification. Squared-radius shoulders are C1; seeds vary tone/grain only. As with existing bounded neighboring-shape queries, an 8 × 8 CSR table stores 224 references, at most 8/average 3.5 candidates per bucket instead of 97 per-pixel tests. Fixed storage is 291+96² Float64 entries and 65+224 Uint16 entries: 76,634 B excluding JS objects/output maps. Trig/sqrt/hashes run only at initialization; sampling allocates nothing and bypasses generic detail. Periodic signed UVs, opaque dielectric M0, four maps plus optional height and existing ownership remain unchanged.

`langtonsant` is an authored 1,024-step Langton-ant snapshot: 122 glossy dark logical-black cells on a rough pale-warm 32 × 32 tiled board, with a raised cream triangle marking the final cell/heading. The actually read [MathWorld Langton’s Ant](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/LangtonsAnt.html) convention turns left 90° on white, right 90° on black, flips the departed cell and advances one unit; do not mix it with the mirrored convention. Starting at (16,16) facing up on an all-white unbounded plane, this offline trajectory ends at (8,8) facing down, with 122 black/226 visited cells. Its entire x=5–24, y=6–22 trajectory stays inside the 32-cell frame. Runtime stores only 32 row bitmaps and the final direction vector, not a simulator or copied image. The nominal 0.32 m tile has 0.01 m cells. Rounded square shoulders and a product of three half-plane ramps keep the compass triangle C1; logical white is rendered pale warm rather than pure white. It is not a QR code, interactive automaton or proof of a 104-step highway/infinite evolution. Each sampler retains one 96² Float64 grain lattice (73,728 B typed storage, excluding JS data/output maps), with O(1) bitmap lookup, allocation-free sampling, no repeated hashes and generic detail bypassed. Periodic signed UVs, opaque dielectric M0, four maps plus optional height and existing ownership remain unchanged.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('langtonsant', {size:512,seed:7,heightMap:true})`. The 1,024 steps/start state define the authored design, not a new public step option. `pentominotiles` packs each of the twelve free pentominoes once into an authored 6 × 10 rectangle, then repeats it 5 × 3 into 30 × 30 cells and 180 glazed pieces. A pentomino is five edge-connected equal squares, with rotations/reflections identified; the actually read [Pentomino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentomino) reference explains the twelve free shapes, 63 fixed orientations and 6 × 10 packing. The layout was solved and checked offline, not copied from an image; A–L are private authored IDs, not conventional letter names. Navy, slate and ivory families have 60 pieces each above rough gray grout. The nominal 0.6 m tile has 0.02 m cells. Smooth neighboring-cell weights merge by whole-piece ID, removing fake internal grid seams; competing IDs tie only inside flat grout, preserving C1 rounded shoulders at concavities and four-cell junctions. This weighted rounding is not an exact geometric offset, installation specification, interactive puzzle or general solver. Initialization retains 900 Uint16 owners, 180 Float64 tones and a 96² Float64 grain lattice: 76,968 B of fixed typed-array storage, excluding JS objects/temporaries/output maps. Sampling allocates nothing, rebuilds no hashes/solver and bypasses generic detail. Periodic signed UVs, opaque dielectric M0, four maps plus optional height and existing ownership remain unchanged.

`pythagorastree` adds four finite glazed-square trees, each with 31 squares (root plus four generations, counts 1/2/4/8/16), fading from red-brown trunks to ivory leaf squares over rough grout. Unlike existing `pythagoreantiles`, it is not a plane-filling 2:1 two-size tiling with five large/five small squares. [Wikipedia Pythagoras tree](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pythagoras_tree_(fractal)>) and [MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/PythagorasTree.html) describe child squares on the legs of an outward isosceles right triangle: child side √2/2 of the parent, child nominal areas summing to parent area. Infinite trees can overlap; area with multiplicity is not generally union area. Exact dyadic-coordinate separating axes verify this authored finite 31-square construction has no interior overlap, 46 nominal corner/edge contacts and root-equivalent area in each generation. `lignumvitae` selects an authored polished dark olive-brown longitudinal lignum-vitae face: fine long grain and softly interleaved pigment remain coplanar, with only sparse short vessels recessed, darker and rougher—not golden Iroko, blood-red Bloodwood, purple Purpleheart or exaggerated zebra stripes. It reuses the complete Iroko/fine-grain core with constructor-only kind/preset selection and unused generic-detail exclusion; the per-point evaluator is verbatim unchanged. All 798 old four-map outputs and seven neighboring woods' 32/512 three-seed five-map outputs remain byte-identical, without new per-sample allocation, hash, trig, sqrt or runtime dependencies. `sateen` selects authored ivory five-harness filling-faced cotton sateen: one isolated warp binder per row and column in a 5×5 repeat, dispersed by a two-step satin counter, with the other four crossings forming continuous filling floats across four warp ends—not adjacent twill, plain weave, crossing-by-crossing beads or the existing purple warp-faced Satin. Only constructor preset selection changes; the former fineTwill flag is renamed fineCloth to include satin structure, and the complete per-point evaluator is unchanged. All 797 old 32px four-map outputs and seven adjacent fabrics' 32/512 three-seed five-map outputs remain byte-identical. The 55×55 yarns, 220×220 fiber frequencies, 5×5×6 float profiles and 128² grain use 16,534 Float64 / 132,272B of tables, not total RAM. Fifty-five is divisible by five, closing the draft at UV seams while avoiding an all-gap alias at 32px without resolution-specific branches. Radius 0.495 < 0.5, continuous floats and C1 yarn shoulders reuse the existing core without new per-sample allocation, hash, trig, sqrt or runtime dependencies. The 0.04m nominal tile, 0.0008 UV-relative relief, ivory palette and roughness 0.45 are authored references, not measured thread count, thickness, dye or luster. `parallelkeys` approximates a top view of double-rounded Form A parallel keys: solid silver-gray long bars with broad flat faces, parallel sides and two curved ends, smoothly beveled into dark, rougher dielectric backing. They are not cylinders, ellipses, square-ended bars, hollow rings or Woodruff segments. It follows the existing hardware seeded-pose and cached-grain pattern, using squared distance to a line segment for a bounded capsule footprint, with no per-sample allocation, hash, trigonometry or square root and no new runtime dependency. The 4×4 six-value poses plus 96² grain total 9,312 Float64 / 74,496B of tables, not total RAM; maximum rotated reach times scale plus jitter is 0.399525 < 0.5, preventing owner boundaries from cutting a key. The 0.12m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief are authored references, not CAD dimensions or displacement in metres. Metal tops remain separate from M0 backing; the factory defaults its metallic factor to 1 to preserve the map and still honors an explicit 0 override. Opaque four-map output, optional height, tint, repeats, cache, native Worker and independent texture ownership are retained. No key mesh, keyway assembly or mechanics is added, and DIN dimensions/tolerances, C45 composition, heat treatment, torque and safety are not certified. Use the root factory `await ProceduralMaterial.create('parallelkeys', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })` and destroy the returned material when its owned textures are no longer needed.

`smithsonite` selects an authored apple-green botryoidal appearance: irregular rounded crowns join into one bounded relief layer, with brighter, smoother crowns and darker, rougher green interstices. It is not a flat green-dot pattern or sky-blue Hemimorphite with pale interstices. It reuses the complete smooth joined-cap core; only constructor preset selection and unused generic-detail exclusion change, with no added per-point allocation, hash, trig, sqrt or runtime dependency. The 0.12m nominal tile and 0.006 UV-relative relief are authored references, not measured crystal dimensions or displacement in metres. `macassarebony` approximates an authored polished longitudinal Macassar-ebony face: dark brown with unequal near-black streaks and fine sparse recessed vessels that are rougher and more occluded. Pigment stays coplanar—not carved grooves, board seams, pale-gold Zebrawood or closed-eye Bocote figure. It reuses the complete Bocote/Zebrawood kernel; constructor-only kind/preset selection chooses a 32×4 warp cache while both old kinds retain 3×5. The per-sample evaluator is verbatim unchanged. The 32×24×4 pores, 32×4 warp, 32×4 width, 64×4 fiber and 128² grain total 19,968 Float64 / 159,744B tables, not total RAM. Maximum band support is 0.39 < 0.5, each signed shoulder equation has a u-derivative lower bound of 1.76 > 0, and maximum vessel half-width/length 0.06/0.31 remain within their owners. Sampling adds no allocation/hash/trig/sqrt or runtime dependency. The 0.18m nominal tile, 0.0016 UV relief and brown palette are authored references, not measured growth rings, wood-fiber dimensions or displacement in meters. Opaque dielectric/M0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership retain their contracts; no board/vessel mesh, transparent holes, varnish layer or directional BRDF, and no species, endgrain/mineral-fill, mechanical/durability, origin/legal-sourcing or safety certification. Related Zebrawood tests now observe actual surfaces rather than copying private hash/noise code.

`serge` approximates authored matte navy balanced 2/2 Serge: equally dyed warp/weft stagger one yarn per row, with continuous two-over/two-under short floats on both axes, broad smooth yarn shoulders and weak grain—not printed diagonal stripes, crossing-by-crossing beads, plain weave or warp-faced 3/1. Constructor-only preset/fineCloth selection reuses the complete Surah/Lyocell kernel; the per-sample evaluator is verbatim unchanged. The 52×52 yarns, 208×208 fiber frequencies and four-step draft use 4×4×6 profiles plus 128² grain: 16,480 Float64 / 131,840B tables, not total RAM. Radius 0.495 stays inside each thread owner; C1 shoulders and signed periods remain, without new per-sample allocation/hash/trig/sqrt or runtime dependencies. Fifty-two yarns avoid the all-gap alias at the supported 32px minimum without a resolution special case. The 0.04m nominal tile, 0.004 UV relief and navy palette are authored references, not measured yarn density, fiber dimensions, thickness in meters or calibrated dye. `garterstitch` approximates an authored warm-cream garter surface: soft horizontal ridges carry staggered curved purl crowns and lower return arcs, uniform dye, weak grain and gentle seeded course wander—not a straight V/bar knitting chart, printed stripes, vertical ribbing, seed-stitch dots or metal. The standalone leaf uses existing cachedNoise/smooth with compact elliptical-ring and half-plane shoulders; three front neighbors and both half-cell return neighbors retain their support, with product unions and exposed underpasses rather than a max crease. The 24-column/20-ridge preset caches 96² grain plus a 24×20 course field: 9696 Float64 / 77,568B tables, not total RAM. No complete intermeshed-yarn/fuzz mesh, elasticity/drape/two-sided garment construction, fiber composition, measured physical gauge or calibrated BRDF is supplied. `woodruffkeys` approximates scattered silver-grey solid Woodruff-key faces: a straight chord and one circular arc bound a shallow disc segment, with seeded orientation, position, size and small tone changes—not coins, triangles, oblong slots or bored washers. Existing periodic cachedNoise/hash/smooth combine circular and half-plane compact C1 shoulders, nearly flat raised metal with weak grain and a dark matte dielectric backing, not transparent gaps. The constructor caches 4×4×6 poses plus 96² grain: 9312 Float64 / 74,496B tables, not total RAM. The rotated whole-disc support plus jitter is 0.434 < 0.5, so owner changes cannot cut a part; no per-sample allocation, hash, trig or sqrt is added. No thickness mesh, shaft/keyway assembly, load/material-grade/DIN/safety certification or photo-calibrated dimensions, color or BRDF is supplied.

`barite` approximates selected opaque pale-cream tabular baryte: locally parallel triples of broad four-sided plates with staggered ends, nearly flat faces smoother than a matte brown mineral host—not narrow blue three-ridged Kyanite, round caps, a tile grid or a color print. It shares the complete existing Kyanite blade sampler; only the original 0.05 face-tilt and 0.08 ridge-height coefficients move to its preset and are captured once by the constructor, while Barite selects 0 / 0.002. Plate half-width 0.09 stays below the nearest-blade owner half-pitch 0.095; maximum rotated bundle support plus jitter is about 0.419992, below the cell-owner half-width 0.5. Smooth product shoulders and signed periods remain. Nominal 0.08m tile and 0.003 UV relief are authored references, not measured crystal dimensions, thickness or meter-unit displacement. Opaque dielectric/M0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership remain unchanged. No transparency/refraction, real crystal mesh/complete specimen, cleavage optics or radial desert-rose cluster, nor composition, origin, value, density, use or safety certification is supplied. Related old Kyanite private-hash/pose assertions are replaced by blind connected-face/PCA transverse profiles detecting three real raised smoother ridges, not an implementation oracle.

`surah` approximates an authored warm copper-colored, balanced 2/2 fine silk-twill surface: two over/two under stepping one yarn per row, with continuous two-pick floats on both axes—not plain weave, warp-faced 3/1, grouped 2×2 basket weave, crossing-by-crossing beads or copper metal. It reuses the complete existing Lyocell-family weave sampler: constructor-only fineCloth/preset selection uses existing whole-run float profiles and equally dyed warp/weft; the per-sample evaluator is verbatim unchanged. The 60×60 yarns, 240×240 fibers and four-step draft use 4×4×6 profiles plus 128² grain: 16,480 Float64 / 131,840B tables, not total RAM; no new per-sample allocation/hash/trig/sqrt or runtime dependency. Radius 0.495 stays inside each thread owner; C1 shoulders and signed UV periods remain. Nominal 0.015m tile, 0.0007 UV relief and warm copper palette are authored references, not measured sett, fiber dimensions, geometry thickness, meter-unit displacement or calibrated dye. Opaque dielectric/M0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership remain unchanged. SILKNOW defines Surah only as soft twilled silk; Première Vision’s Silk Twill provides the two-over/two-under reference and its viewed photograph is blue, not copper. This does not make every Surah 2/2 or copper-colored. No silk-composition, origin, hand, durability or safety certification, true reverse-side/drape/transmission, directional silk luster or new sheen BSDF. Sixty yarns retain complete four-step repeats without the all-gap 32px sampling alias of 64 yarns; the adjusted nominal tile keeps authored yarn density unchanged, with no minimum-resolution special case.

`bocote` approximates a selected polished longitudinal Bocote face with a golden-brown body, high-contrast dark-brown to near-black grain and locally closed eye figure—not a claim that all Bocote has eyes, an endgrain anatomy diagram, pasted concentric targets or raised rings. It reuses the complete Zebrawood sampling kernel with only constructor preset selection; stronger authored phase warping folds longitudinal grain back into closed contours. Light and dark figure remain coplanar; only sparse short longitudinal vessels recess. A 16×8×4 pore table plus 3×5 warp, 24×4 width, 64×4 fiber and 128² grain total 17,263 Float64 values / 138,104 bytes of tables, not total RAM. The 0.24 m nominal tile and 0.0016 UV relief are not measured grain spacing, pore diameter, meter-valued displacement or wood thickness.
